newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev ends firmer amid dollar-bearish mood.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev ends firmer amid dollar-bearish mood.

text.p: Foreign currency supply topped demand on the Bulgarian interbank forex market, boosting the lev to 222-223 per dollar at close from about 225.50/226 in the morning and 224-225 at the previous close, dealers said.
"The current very high yield on lev-denominated investments encouraged large-scale dollar offers by banks and final clients alike but demand was very low," a commercial bank dealer said.
The central bank (BNB) last week raised its main interest rate to 25 percent monthly or 300 percent annually from 108 percent in a bid to restore confidence in the fragile national currency.
The BNB launched dollar sales at 225.00/50 lev in the morning and offset a potential lev's fall towards 230 due to the longer value date of today's spot-deals, traders said.
"Commercial banks and end customers followed suit and further boosted (dollar) supply, which helped the lev to gain to 222 amid a strong dollar-bearish mood," another dealer said.

According to dealers a gradual rate cut would probably not increase pressure on the lev drastically. Central bank governor Lyubomir Filipov has said that the record high rate could be considered a temporary measure. @
"But if the rate is lowered sharply the lev will fall quickly," another dealer said.

The lev's stability would largely hinge on a possible decisison by the International Monetary Fund to release a delayed $115 million second tranche under its funding agreement with Bulgaria, traders said.
The tranche was postponed from September until Bulgaria adequately meets IMF's funding requirements concerning closure of loss-makers. @
Local media on Thursday quoted Filipov as saying in Washington that Bulgaria now stands a very high chance to win the tranche. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
